source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies the concurrent estimand and explains that, with deterministic availability, doubly robust estimators do not obtain the purported NCC efficiency gain absent additional structure.
The paper establishes design-based finite-population IPW/AIPW theory for general adaptive designs, including nonexchangeable units, variable propensities, and martingale-based inference.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies honest confidence intervals for linear functionals over convex regression classes under Gaussian errors, using worst-case bias and modulus-based optimality calculations.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 32(5), 2004 author-hosted article copy
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops between-class and ordered moduli for expected-length lower bounds and constant-factor adaptive confidence intervals for linear functionals.
The article concerns an augmented RCT with external controls, estimates an expected confounding-bias quantity, and selects dynamic borrowing weights under a prespecified bias-tolerance cap.

The paper studies minimax design and estimation risk for finite-population randomized experiments with unrestricted designs and estimators, rather than honest NCC interval length under calendar drift.
The paper defines concurrent cohorts in adaptive platform trials, separates randomized from nonrandomized NCC information, and shows that time adjustment may be insufficient in adaptive designs.

The paper derives minimax confidence-interval-length lower bounds and oracle constructions for combining RCT and observational data under a bounded confounding-bias model, plus an adaptation impossibility result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the clipped intersection by a provably nonempty observed-data kernel, then re-prove its coverage and expected-length bound; either add a full-parameter-space fallback with a tail-length analysis or impose a deterministic score-range condition that rules out empty intersections.
Define a concurrent-only procedure class and its minimax expected-length value, then state and prove the Gamma-vac equality or inequality against that explicit benchmark.

Add Chen, Zhang, and Ye’s minimax CI-length theorem and Marschner and Schou’s cohort-based adaptive-platform analysis to related work, explaining precisely why their model classes do not subsume the proposed fixed-schedule TV experiment.

recommended_next_step: Revise the interval construction and vacuous-drift benchmark, then rerun novelty review with the two missing closest published comparators incorporated.
